column5: ablative absolute with a perfect participle -> postquam + the noun in the nominative + perfect indicative (passive for transitive verbs, so no agent is guessed; deponents active). voice=active: active perfect with the main clause's subject (Check)
ablative absolute with a present participle -> dum + the noun in the nominative + present indicative

gerundive of obligation / passive periphrastic (+ sum): a dative agent becomes the subject of dēbeō + active infinitive, the gerundive's noun its object; without an agent dēbeō + passive infinitive (the meaning stays exact); gerund without agent kept
supine of purpose -> ut + subjunctive after the main verb (present after a present/future main verb, imperfect after a past one)
future participle + sum -> future tense; + a past tense of sum -> volō (imperfect) + infinitive
historic infinitive (a sentence without a finite verb) -> imperfect indicative
cum + pluperfect subjunctive -> postquam + perfect indicative; cum + imperfect subjunctive -> dum + present indicative
a relative clause inside a relative clause that ends the sentence -> a new sentence with the antecedent noun
sentences longer than `words` words are split at et/sed/nam/atque between two finite clauses (et/atque dropped)
accusative + infinitive after verbs of saying and thinking: kept, marked with a note

with the original-language cue: rewrite = the rewrite of the Latin itself when it is clean (no Fix, tier ceiling met, meaning >= 60 %, no construction left), else the original's translation (EN/ES -> LA at fidelity 3) when that one is clean; original = the original's translation first
